# Armagetron Advanced for macOS — v0.4.0-2.0

This release adds a built-in video recorder with instant replay, and a batch of
HUD, cockpit, resource and sound fixes.

## Highlights

- **Native Recorder**: record gameplay to MP4, and save the last 30 seconds on a
  keypress with no re-encoding (Medal-style instant replay).
- **Hardware-encoded video** (HEVC or H.264) with a Quality setting, resolution
  cap and codec choice. HEVC records at native resolution on Apple Silicon.
- **Modded Settings** menu: HUD cockpit browser, font options and the recorder,
  all reachable in game.

## New Features

### Native Recorder

- **Take recording**: bind a key to *Record toggle* to start and stop writing an
  MP4 to disk. Recording streams straight to disk, so memory use does not grow
  with the length of the take.
- **Instant replay**: a rolling buffer keeps the last 30 seconds already encoded
  in memory. Press the clip key (default `C`) to write the last 30 seconds to an
  MP4. The clip is a pass-through mux of the buffered samples — it does not
  re-encode, so saving is quick and does not disturb the game.
- **Audio**: takes include the game's mixed soundtrack. The recorder taps the mix
  before any muting, so recordings keep their audio even when the speakers are
  muted.
- **Quality**: Low / Medium / High / Ultra, which sets the video bitrate. The
  menu shows the resulting Mbps for the current resolution and frame rate.
- **Codec**: HEVC (default) or H.264. HEVC is smaller and its hardware encoder is
  the only one that can record above 4K; H.264 is more compatible but its rate
  control is weaker on this platform.
- **Max height**: 720p, 1080p, 1440p or Native. Native is captured at full window
  resolution up to the hardware limit (4096 px wide for H.264, 8192 for HEVC).
- **Frame rate**: 30 or 60 fps, independent of the render rate — the game may run
  far faster, and the recorder simply skips the extra frames.
- **Clip length** and **Target size** settings, plus a Storage folder you can
  point anywhere.
- New `MOVIE_*` settings, so everything above is scriptable and persists across
  restarts.

### Modded Settings

- Added the **Modded Settings** menu, opened with a key (default `-`) while in
  game: recorder options, the HUD cockpit browser, font controls, text width and
  the HUD map toggle.
- **Cockpit browser**: pick the HUD cockpit, its version and which parts of it to
  draw, with a live preview.

### HUD and cockpits

- Needle-style meters in the HUD gauges, and the classic cockpit now matches the
  0.2.9 layout.
- Shipped a forked **Pink Plus** cockpit.
- The cockpit file is re-read on reload instead of reusing the cached document.

### Rendering

- New **FONT_STRETCH** setting for wider text, exposed in Modded Settings.
- The floor colour default is now a dark grey (0.2).

### Resources

- Resources are fetched in the background; the repositories are consulted before
  a file's own URI. Synchronous stalls on the resource thread are gone.
- Downloaded textures are verified by their resource path.
- The resource fetch worker is joined at exit, avoiding a shutdown race.

### macOS

- Cockpit files can be deployed into an installed client without a rebuild
  (`macos-deploy-cockpit.sh`).
- Self-contained bundles run on other machines.

## Improvements

- A fresh install is silent: music no longer starts until it is asked for
  (`MUSIC_ACTIVE` is honoured, and the default is off).

## Bug Fixes

- **Recorder**: fixed a crash on stopping a recording, caused by an Objective-C
  exception escaping into the game loop, and by freeing the encoder while it was
  still finishing. The writer is now finalised safely, off the render thread.
- **Recorder**: fixed a freeze when saving a clip. Muxing now runs on a
  background thread, and the writer's inputs are finished correctly so it cannot
  stall.
- **Recorder**: fixed the framerate staying low for several seconds after
  returning from a hidden window; capture now pauses while the window is not
  presenting and resumes without a catch-up burst.
- **Recorder**: selecting Native resolution could silently fall back to a
  software encoder (past 4096 px wide with H.264) and tank the framerate. The
  size is now capped per codec so hardware encoding is kept.
- **Shutdown**: fixed a crash in font teardown at exit, and in the GL clear path
  before a window exists.
- **HUD**: player colours above 15 survive opening Player Setup.
- **Rendering**: invalid sizes no longer reach the font cache.

## Known Issues

- H.264 ignores the Quality setting on this platform and encodes at a high, fixed
  rate. Use HEVC for working quality control and native-resolution recording.
- The app is **not signed or notarised**. After unzipping, right-click the app
  and choose **Open** once, and macOS will allow it from then on.
